AWS applied the offset against the Nov marketplace settlement and that produced a negative-amount adjustment on the invoice that your payments team is now holding pending tax treatment.

Can you confirm what evidence you need from us to allow the payout to be reissued and for Redwood to treat this as a seller-side credit (i.e., not additional taxable revenue to Redwood)? The buyer is in Ireland and DataStream is an Irish entity — we expect reverse-charge to apply, but AWS has flagged a VAT mismatch and held the payout.

I can attach the original invoice and the signed credit note if that helps. Also cc'ing aws-marketplace billing (we received their notice but the contact asked us to coordinate with Redwood).

Attachments: DSI_invoice_NOV2026.pdf (original invoice)

Thanks — appreciate a quick path forward, we have a collections hold that is delaying downstream payouts to our engineers.

Hi Liam,

Thanks — I can confirm why AWS flagged this. For marketplace offsets we require a short evidence set to permit reclassification and release of withheld funds:
1) Signed seller credit form (fillable PDF) naming Redwood as the affected marketplace host and referencing the marketplace adjustment ID (if available).
2) Original invoice (you already attached) + buyer VAT number.
3) Seller VAT/Tax registration certificate (govt-issued) showing DataStream Ireland Ltd VAT ID.
4) A short note confirming whether the credit is customer-requested or seller-initiated; if customer-requested we need the customer email thread or DocuSign showing acceptance.

I've attached our billing evidence checklist and the seller-credit template for you to complete and return. Once we receive all 4 items we will:
- Open a manual ledger correction (internal ledger ticket)
- Request AWS marketplace ops to reprocess the settlement (Karthik will lead)
- Clear the Redwood-held payout to your registered payout bank after final validation

Attachments: redwood_billing_evidence_checklist.csv, redwood_seller_credit_template.pdf

Note on VAT handling: If DataStream is an EU-registered entity and the buyer is also an EU entity that provided a VAT ID, reverse-charge can apply; we will still need the VAT registration cert to avoid Redwood being liable for VAT on the adjustment. If the buyer is non-EU, we may need additional customs/tax paperwork.

EOD turnaround once docs are complete — please escalate to your legal/finance team if needed.

Best,
Neha
